plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $9, I will bid exactly $9 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay a fair price determined by the second-highest bid.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' actions. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds risk without benefit, and bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for opponent behavior, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $40, ensuring I maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ($32) ensures I never overpay - if I win, I pay less than my value (profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me. There's no incentive to bid higher (risk of overpaying) or lower (risk of losing profitable opportunities). I'll bid my true value.
